newsitem.title: UK: Laura Ashley slips further, forecasts cut.
newsitem.headline: Laura Ashley slips further, forecasts cut.

text.p: British retailer Laura Ashley Holdings Plc saw its shares slip further on Thursday, after warning profits this year would fall short of expectations.
Analysts said they would revise profit forecasts for the current year to around 20 million stg from between 22 and 23 million.
Laura Ashley, with operations in the Europe and North America, is in the process of restructuring to produce better returns from its fashion and home furnishing businesses.
Chief executive Ann Iverson said the recovery programme was still on track, but the group had over bought stock and would have to mark prices down to clear the backlog.
The shares were down 41 pence at 104 pence by 1345 GMT.
Analysts said the stock had been a victim of over-hyped expectations.
"It's a difficult and complicated recovery and market expectations were too high," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at Mees Pierson.
